M8-Ps-031.rationale: The title “A Prayer by David.” (web:Ps.17.0 = oshb:Ps.17.1) opens with תְּפִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד, tefillah le-David, a superscription genre label (tier-1 opener class) echoed within the same MT verse by תְפִלָּתִ֑י, 'my prayer,' in “Give ear to my prayer that doesn't go out of deceitful lips” (web:Ps.17.1). The vocative-imperative cluster “Hear, Yahweh, my righteous plea. Give ear...” (web:Ps.17.1) and the jussive petition “Let my sentence come out of your presence” (web:Ps.17.2) open a plea for a verdict that the psalmist grounds in sworn self-testimony through “My steps have held fast to your paths. My feet have not slipped” (web:Ps.17.5), so the appeal and its supporting testimony read as one continuous unit addressed to Yahweh, with the next vocative-imperative cluster resuming at web:Ps.17.6.
M8-Ps-031.rejected_alternative: Isolating web:Ps.17.1-Ps.17.2 as its own strophe would sever the verdict plea from the innocence testimony that syntactically sustains it through web:Ps.17.5.
observed_substrate_signals: title תְּפִלָּ֗ה לְדָ֫וִ֥ד (oshb:Ps.17.1) is a genre-label superscription, tier-1 opener class
the title's prayer-noun is echoed by תְפִלָּתִ֑י within the same MT verse (oshb:Ps.17.1)
imperative verbs cluster at the verse's open (“Hear... Give ear...”, web:Ps.17.1); the next such cluster sits at web:Ps.17.6
M8-Ps-031.device_notes: This psalm's rows nest under one Psalm-17 parent.

M8-Ps-032.rationale: A fresh vocative-imperative cluster opens the strophe — “I have called on you, for you will answer me, God. Turn your ear to me. Hear my speech” (web:Ps.17.6) — echoing the psalm's opening plea (web:Ps.17.1) with a second petition cycle. The imperatives continue through protective imagery, “Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings” (web:Ps.17.8), whose object clause runs on into “from the wicked who oppress me, my deadly enemies, who surround me” (web:Ps.17.9) — the enemies appear here as the target of 'Hide me... from,' not yet as an independent descriptive subject, which keeps web:Ps.17.9 inside this petition rather than opening the third-person indictment at web:Ps.17.10.
M8-Ps-032.rejected_alternative: Splitting web:Ps.17.6-Ps.17.7 from web:Ps.17.8-Ps.17.9 would break the one imperative sentence that runs from 'Hide me' to its enemy-naming object clause.
observed_substrate_signals: vocative “God” + imperative cluster (“Turn your ear... Hear my speech”) opens web:Ps.17.6, mirroring the imperative cluster opening web:Ps.17.1
the object clause of “Hide me... under the shadow of your wings” (web:Ps.17.8) continues syntactically into web:Ps.17.9's enemy description

M8-Ps-033.rationale: The subject shifts from direct address of Yahweh to third-person description of the enemies — “They close up their callous hearts. With their mouth they speak proudly” (web:Ps.17.10) — continuing through the lion simile “He is like a lion that is greedy of his prey... lurking in secret places” (web:Ps.17.12); direct address of Yahweh resumes at web:Ps.17.13 (“Arise, Yahweh, confront him.”), which begins the following strophe.
M8-Ps-033.rejected_alternative: Grouping this third-person indictment with the imprecation that follows would obscure the address shift back to Yahweh that opens the next strophe.
observed_substrate_signals: third-person verbs (“They close up”, “they speak”, “He is like a lion”) replace the second-person address of the prior strophe across web:Ps.17.10-Ps.17.12
the vocative 'Yahweh' + imperative 'Arise... confront him' reopen direct address at web:Ps.17.13

M8-Ps-034.rationale: The vocative “Yahweh” and imperative cluster “Arise... confront him. Cast him down. Deliver my soul” (web:Ps.17.13) open the closing strophe's imprecation, which runs through the description of “men of the world, whose portion is in this life” (web:Ps.17.14) before the contrastive turn “As for me, I shall see your face in righteousness” (web:Ps.17.15) closes the psalm; the disjunctive 'As for me' answers 'men of the world... in this life' with the psalmist's own hope, so the imprecation and its resolving contrast belong to one closing movement rather than separate strophes.
M8-Ps-034.rejected_alternative: Separating the imprecation from its closing contrast would divide one argument that moves from the fate of the wicked to the psalmist's own hope.
observed_substrate_signals: vocative “Yahweh” + imperative cluster (“Arise... confront him... Cast him down... Deliver my soul”) opens web:Ps.17.13
the contrastive “As for me” at web:Ps.17.15 answers “men of the world... in this life” at web:Ps.17.14
